claims.claim_text: Better outcomes come from whether one proposes or receives, not talent or luck.
claims.evidence_quote: l.6: "nothing to do with talent, luck, or even the quality of their choices"
claims.reasoning: Source states the insight explains consistently better outcomes and explicitly excludes talent and luck, so the rephrase is identical in meaning.

claims.claim_text: In 1962 Gale and Shapley sought pairings no unmatched pair would break.
claims.evidence_quote: l.12: "In 1962, mathematician-economists David Gale and Lloyd Shapley" sought "no two unmatched people would prefer each other over their assigned partners"
claims.reasoning: Year, both names, and the stability goal all match the source exactly.

claims.claim_text: Deferred acceptance gives each proposer their best stable partner, each receiver their worst.
claims.evidence_quote: l.16: "proposers get their best possible partner among all stable matchings, while receivers get their worst possible partner among all stable matchings"
claims.reasoning: The best-for-proposer / worst-for-receiver result is stated verbatim in meaning; algorithm name appears at l.15.

claims.claim_text: The gap is systematically, provably, mathematically extreme, not slight.
claims.evidence_quote: l.18: "it systematically, provably, mathematically extreme" and "isn't just slightly better or worse"
claims.reasoning: Direct paraphrase preserving both the emphasis and the denial that the gap is slight.

claims.claim_text: Real situations skip the exact algorithm but share the propose-respond structure.
claims.evidence_quote: l.22: "most real-world situations don't follow the exact Gale-Shapley algorithm. But they share the fundamental structure"
claims.reasoning: Both the denial of exact use and the shared-structure claim are stated in source.

claims.claim_text: Netflix, phones, jobs, friendships illustrate pre-decided pursuit versus presented selection.
claims.evidence_quote: l.28-34: the four Netflix / phone / job / friend questions contrasting deciding versus scrolling or choosing displayed options
claims.reasoning: All four examples are present in source with the same pursue-versus-select contrast.

claims.claim_text: For most of these, most of us are receivers choosing from presentations.
claims.evidence_quote: l.36: "For most of these, most of us are receivers. We're choosing from what's presented"
claims.reasoning: Near-verbatim restatement including both hedges (most of these, most of us).

claims.claim_text: Receivers get acceptable, good-enough outcomes, never terrible ones.
claims.evidence_quote: l.40: "isn't that you get terrible outcomes. You don't. You get acceptable ones. Good enough ones"
claims.reasoning: Both the denial of terrible outcomes and the acceptable/good-enough characterization match, negation polarity intact.

claims.claim_text: Decent differs from best-serving; structure favors proposers without conspiracy.
claims.evidence_quote: l.42-44: "'decent' isn't the same as 'what would actually serve you best'" and "Not because of some conspiracy, but because of the mathematical properties"
claims.reasoning: Both halves are stated in source, including the explicit denial of conspiracy.

claims.claim_text: Fine feelings block revolt-driving dissatisfaction; quiet under-service stays stable.
claims.evidence_quote: l.46: "because your outcomes feel fine, you never develop the dissatisfaction that would push you to become a proposer"
claims.reasoning: The causal chain from feeling fine to no revolt to stability is stated in source.

claims.claim_text: Intention is needed to propose, yet intention develops only through proposing.
claims.evidence_quote: l.56: "You need intention to propose, but you develop intention through proposing"
claims.reasoning: Verbatim in meaning; this is the source's stated trap.

claims.claim_text: Receiver choices reveal the least-disliked option, never freely pursued desire.
claims.evidence_quote: l.54: "Those choices just reveal which option you dislike least among what's available"
claims.reasoning: Paraphrase preserves the least-disliked-available versus freely-pursued contrast.

claims.claim_text: Algorithmic songs and swiped partners leave wants as reactions to offerings.
claims.evidence_quote: l.58: "just the best matches from what the algorithm served you"; l.60: "did you swipe through available profiles"
claims.reasoning: Both the music-algorithm and dating-swipe examples are in source with the same reaction-to-offerings point.

claims.claim_text: The intention muscle builds progressively; no jump from Netflix to life vision.
claims.evidence_quote: l.66: "You can't jump straight from 'I pick from what Netflix recommends' to 'I have a clear vision for my life's work.' The muscle of intention and initiative builds progressively"
claims.reasoning: Both the denial of instant jump and the progressive-build claim match.

claims.claim_text: Tonight: name the hour's want (laugh, learn, calm, challenge), then seek it.
claims.evidence_quote: l.68-70: "decide intentionally what you actually want from the next hour" with "laugh? Learn something? Feel calm? Be challenged?"
claims.reasoning: Exercise, specificity requirement, and all four example wants are stated in source.

claims.claim_text: Patterns become preferences, preferences values; values are practiced into, not thought into.
claims.evidence_quote: l.72-74: "Those patterns become preferences. Those preferences become values" and "You can't think your way into values. You have to practice your way into them"
claims.reasoning: The full chain and the practice-not-thought contrast are stated verbatim in meaning.

claims.claim_text: Major decisions usually evaluate presented options; receiving feels like agency.
claims.evidence_quote: l.80-82: "Most people, most of the time, are evaluating presented options. This feels like agency because you're choosing. But you're choosing as a receiver"
claims.reasoning: Hedges (most people, most of the time) and the feels-like-agency point are preserved.

claims.claim_text: Proposers of work, partners, and cities win systematically from structural position.
claims.evidence_quote: l.84: proposers "end up with systematically better outcomes"; l.86: "Because they're on the other side of a structure"
claims.reasoning: Work, partner, and city proposer examples plus the structural (not smarter/luckier) cause are all stated.

claims.claim_text: Platforms take optimal outcomes (attention, data, money); users keep good-enough engagement.
claims.evidence_quote: l.94: "the platforms get optimal outcomes (your attention, your data, your money), and you get outcomes that are good enough to keep you participating"
claims.reasoning: Both sides of the split and all three extracted items (attention, data, money) match.

claims.claim_text: Staying wins because leaving feels harder; stability is resistance to change.
claims.evidence_quote: l.96: "You stay because leaving feels harder than accepting 'good enough.' That's stability (resistance to change)"
claims.reasoning: Cause and parenthetical definition are verbatim in meaning.

claims.claim_text: Understanding changes nothing; one must actually switch positions against designed defaults.
claims.evidence_quote: l.100-102: "The structural disadvantage of being a receiver doesn't go away because you understand it. You have to actually switch positions" plus "environment is designed to keep us receiving"
claims.reasoning: The denial that understanding suffices and the switch-positions demand are both stated.

claims.claim_text: Propose means: decide before seeing options, pursue specifics, create openings, accept friction.
claims.evidence_quote: l.104-108: the four bullets "Deciding intentionally what you want before seeing what's available" through "Accepting the friction of going against default flows"
claims.reasoning: All four listed behaviors match the source's four bullets in order and meaning.

claims.claim_text: Ask what one wants before every major decision and most minor ones, then act.
claims.evidence_quote: l.110: "asking 'what do I actually want?' before every major decision and most minor ones"
claims.reasoning: Scope quantifiers (every major, most minor) are preserved exactly.

claims.claim_text: Most will refuse: effortful, comfortable, and forgetful of what to propose.
claims.evidence_quote: l.112: "Most people won't do this. It's effortful. The receiver position is comfortable enough" plus "have lost the capacity to even know what they'd want"
claims.reasoning: All three reasons (effort, comfort, lost capacity) are stated in source.

claims.claim_text: The dynamic is confirmed; the open question is whether the reader acts.
claims.evidence_quote: l.116-118: "The question isn't whether this dynamic exists" and "The question is whether you're willing to do something about it"
claims.reasoning: Both halves mirror the source's closing two questions.

claims.claim_text: Start tomorrow morning small, practice a week, then scale to big decisions.
claims.evidence_quote: l.122: "Start with tomorrow morning"; l.130: "Do this for a week with small things"; l.132: "Then scale up"
claims.reasoning: The three-stage sequence (morning start, week of small, scale up) is stated across the cited passages.

claims.claim_text: Morning: decide the first hour's want before the phone, then pursue it.
claims.evidence_quote: l.124-126: "Before you check your phone, decide intentionally: what do you actually want from the first hour of your day?"
claims.reasoning: Phone-first prohibition, first-hour scope, and pursue-it follow-through all match.

claims.claim_text: Log small satisfactions a week, then decide work, love, and problems first.
claims.evidence_quote: l.130: "Notice what actually satisfies you versus what just filled time"; l.132: "Before looking at job postings, decide" / "Before swiping" / "Before browsing products, decide what problem"
claims.reasoning: Week of small things plus the decide-first ordering for jobs, dating, and products are stated; 'log' compresses the notice/track instruction harmlessly.

claims.claim_text: Muscle enables intentions, intentions values; proposers win from the other side.
claims.evidence_quote: l.134-138: "The practice builds the muscle. The muscle enables larger intentions. Larger intentions become values" and "Because they're on the other side of the equation"
claims.reasoning: Chain and payoff restate the source's own closing recap with identical meaning.

claims.claim_text: Entertainment drill: three weeks of naming, seeking, and protecting intention with timers.
claims.evidence_quote: l.148-162: Week 1 name intention, Week 2 seek intentionally, Week 3 protect intention with timer
claims.reasoning: All three weekly phases and the timer detail match the appendix.

claims.claim_text: Shopping drill: exact problem, 3-5 must-haves, 24-hour rule over $100.
claims.evidence_quote: l.167: "Define the problem"; l.168: "What 3-5 features"; l.171: "For anything over $100, wait a day"
claims.reasoning: Problem-first, 3-5 count, and $100/24-hour numbers are exact.

claims.claim_text: Jobs drill: two-week energy map, five non-negotiables, apply only at 4-of-5 matches.
claims.evidence_quote: l.181: "For two weeks, note what tasks"; l.183: "Write 5 non-negotiables"; l.189: "Only apply to roles that match at least 4 of your 5 criteria"
claims.reasoning: Two weeks, five criteria, and the 4-of-5 threshold are exact.

claims.claim_text: Relationships drill: specific intention plus 3-5 must-align values, seek and filter.
claims.evidence_quote: l.196: "Write your relationship intention"; l.197: "What 3-5 values absolutely must align?"
claims.reasoning: Intention-first, 3-5 values, and intentional seeking all match.

claims.claim_text: Micro-practices: 5-minute morning trio, 5-minute review, 10-second pause.
claims.evidence_quote: l.208-209: "Morning routine (5 minutes)" with "three intentions"; l.212: "Evening review (5 minutes)"; l.218: "pause for 10 seconds"
claims.reasoning: All three durations and the trio/three-intentions detail are exact.

claims.claim_text: Three-column journal for 30 days: situation, mode, outcome; start small.
claims.evidence_quote: l.224-229: "three columns" Situation/Mode/Outcome and "After 30 days, you'll see the pattern clearly"
claims.reasoning: Column count, column names, and 30-day span are exact.
